messages.text: Russell posts statement to 'speak from the heart'

metadata.summary: George Russell has posted a statement on social media to "speak from the heart" after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver posts statement to 'speak from the heart' after Kimi Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver posts statement to 'speak from the heart' after Kimi Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix Mercedes' George Russell took to social media on Monday after not speaking to the media after Sunday's Mexico City GP, where his team-mate Kimi Antonelli became world champion; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo GP at 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 2 November 2026 20:31, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle believes Kimi Antonelli winning the world title could trigger an 'overdrive' for George Russell, or it's 'game over' for the Mercedes team-mate George Russell has posted a statement on social media to "speak from the heart" after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff revealed Russell was "distraught" in Mexico and went home after congratulating Antonelli on becoming world champion. The FIA gave Mercedes a €5,000 (£4,173) fine as Russell missed his mandatory media duties post-race, but the British driver has made his own first public comments on Monday. messages.text: Edwards: Borthwick turned down my offer to work with England

metadata.summary: Renowned defence coach Shaun Edwards says England boss Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with the side at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.
metadata.content: England rugby: Shaun Edwards says Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with side at 2027 World Cup | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England rugby: Shaun Edwards says Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with side at 2027 World Cup Shaun Edwards told Steve Borthwick that he would be "assistant kit man" if required but England head coach happy with his current staff; Borthwick's side play Australia at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium on Sunday, before clashes with Japan and New Zealand across the next two weekends Monday 2 November 2026 20:21, UK Image: Shaun Edwards says England head coach Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with the side at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. Renowned defence coach Shaun Edwards says England boss Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with the side at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia. Edwards ended a six-year spell with France - during which Les Bleus won three Six Nations, including back-to-back in 2025 and 2026 - earlier this year. The 60-year-old worked with the England women's team on a short-term basis and has now moved onto Argentina's staff until the end of next year's World Cup, which runs across October and November. messages.text: England to host South Africa live on Sky Sports in Netball World Cup prep

metadata.summary: England's Vitality Roses will host South Africa in a three-Test netball series in February, with all matches live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: England to host South Africa in three-Test netball series live on Sky Sports in February as World Cup preparation | Netball News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England to host South Africa in three-Test netball series live on Sky Sports in February as World Cup preparation Vitality Roses will tackle the Proteas twice in London and once in Leicester in February 2027; games will help sides prepare for Netball World Cup in Australia in August and September; England edged South Africa this summer to reach Commonwealth Games semi-finals at opponents' expense Monday 2 November 2026 18:00, UK Image: England will play South Africa in London and Leicester in February 2027 as they build for the Netball World Cup in Australia (image credit: Ben Lumley) England's Vitality Roses will host South Africa in a three-Test netball series in February, with all matches live on Sky Sports. The games will serve as preparation for the 2027 World Cup in Australia across late August and early September. England, currently third in the world rankings, will take on fifth-placed South Africa at Wembley Arena in London on February 6 and 7 before the series concludes at Leicester's Mattioli Arena on February 10. messages.text: Carney urges RFL to adopt strategic plan after England's World Cup exits

metadata.summary: Brian Carney has urged the Rugby Football League (RFL) to get serious about its ambitions to strengthen the domestic game in England by implementing a strategic plan.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Brian Carney urges RFL to implement plan to fix sport's key issues after England's exits | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: Brian Carney urges RFL to implement plan to fix sport's key issues after England's exits England men and women were knocked out in group stages of Rugby League World Cup; the RFL has appointed a panel of ex-players to hold discussions on future of the national sides Brian Carney Rugby League Expert & Columnist Monday 2 November 2026 20:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carney believes England's performances at the Rugby League World Cup are a "symptom" of the sport's bigger issues Brian Carney has urged the Rugby Football League (RFL) to get serious about its ambitions to strengthen the domestic game in England by implementing a strategic plan. Following England men's and women's teams exits from the Rugby League World Cup, the RFL established an advisory panel consisting of multiple former Great Britain and England players to hold discussions and plot out a roadmap to improve the international game. In February, the RFL also released 144 strategic recommendations detailing key issues within rugby league in England, relating to governance, financing, and improving player pathways. metadata.summary: Sky Sports pundit Mark Webster says Fallon Sherrock "should not have been selected to play" for Netflix 'Beat Luke Littler' in which she claimed the winning prize of £501,000.
metadata.content: Beat Luke Littler: Fallon Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' in Netflix show but you can't blame 'Queen of the Palace' | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Beat Luke Littler: Fallon Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' in Netflix show but you can't blame 'Queen of the Palace' Fallon Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' for Netflix show 'Beat Luke Littler' according to Sky Sports pundit Mark Webster; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Mark Webster Darts Expert & Columnist Monday 2 November 2026 16:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fallon Sherrock beat 'The Nuke' at the 'Beat Luke Littler' event to claim a £501,000 prize! Credit: Netflix Sky Sports pundit Mark Webster says Fallon Sherrock "should not have been selected to play" for Netflix 'Beat Luke Littler' in which she claimed the winning prize of £501,000. Sherrock overcame the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501 to claim the second biggest prize in darts history . But this was not Sherrock's first foray into the limelight as she created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round in December 2019, and she went on to break several other barriers in the game, including becoming the first woman to reach the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts. metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic missed a big chance to strengthen his push for a place at the end-of-year ATP Finals after a loss ‌to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.
metadata.content: Novak Djokovic: After shock defeat in Basel former world No 1 heads to Paris Masters in race to make ATP Finals in Turin | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Novak Djokovic: After shock defeat in Basel former world No 1 heads to Paris Masters in race to make ATP Finals in Turin Novak Djokovic needs at the very least a semi-final at the Paris Masters to have a chance to make the ATP Finals in Turin; a final appearance would likely do it, and a title would surely do it; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2 Monday 2 November 2026 13:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Swiss Indoors match between Novak Djokovic and Jan-Lennard Struff Novak Djokovic missed a big chance to strengthen his push for a place at the end-of-year ATP Finals after a loss ‌to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. Defeat has left the Serb with precious few opportunities to make up ground in the race to Turin. Back ‌in Basel for the first time in 15 years, 39-year-old Djokovic fell 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (5-7) in the second round, his first defeat by German veteran Struff in nine meetings.
